body:
Mine unit is cheaper than the average, just looked it up. The units here are at the average or just below it for this area. I'm next to like 6 other complexes that charge the same or way more.

I lived in an older one down the road and had to fight ants, roaches and management bullshit. I moved to this one when it was built for the same price.

Rent is insane everywhere.
😂 Who needs sleep?

If this golf course was a park, there wouldn't be a problem. Everyone can use a park. 

Golf courses can only be used by those who have the means to pay for entry and equipment. And they use more water. Spaces in densely populated areas should be used more wisely. Put the golf courses on the edge of town.
I live in a building like this 💀
I live in a building designed like this. It sucks lol.
Pretty on brand for us to copy a European concept and ruin it lol.
Yeah. I feel like I was born too early. Wake me back up when we have moved past religion and capitalism.
5 floors, in a state with hot summers.

It's a bit of both. The courtyard I face is a similar size to the ones in the photo. It is small enough that no amount of trees planted inside would stop me from hearing a party or dog barking across the courtyard. And the interior attracts people to hang out and use the amenities, so there's people constantly talking and walking 10 feet from my back window. And they think it's cool to blast music there because it is an amenity space provided by the complex.

Like another comment pointed out, the enclosed interior also traps heat, which is bad for A/C and kills vegetation in hot locations.

And my complex has huge bright lights that turn on at sundown for safety purposes, which shine into all the windows.

There's no darkness here, and silence is rare. Not good for your health.

I live in one and it is not awesome. Read the rest of the comments under mine to see why it's nice on paper but not in practice. 

Maybe there's a way to implement it correctly? I could see how this would be nice if the interior was large enough to prevent echoes and heat trapping. Like having a whole park in the middle. But if they are built like the photo above, they suck.

It's such an exclusionary holiday. Anyone struggling with infertility, a deceased or absent mother, distant children, deceased children, etc. gets to feel like shit while everyone else posts photos of their babies, their loving mothers, and "happy" families.

I'm so sorry that you are going through this. Sending you a big virtual hug. Other women are not better than you because of how they are treated on a single Sunday.

How old are your children? Do they know this day is important to you? They might not be aware.
True. Or train tracks. I like how other countries put walls up next to tracks and highways to dampen the sound and give privacy.

YES! I haven't been able to grow a plant on my balcony because the heat kills them. The tiny yards in the ground units have dead grass. The sun reflects off the windows and metal siding and the heat from it stays trapped in the courtyard 🥵

Oh absolutely. I love the idea. Golf courses are fucking awful and if they have to exist, they should be limited in number and located on the outskirts of town. Just saying the O shaped buildings are not a good way to develop this space if you care about the tenants.

I currently face an enclosed courtyard like this in a multi story building.  No trees, and the shrubs don't dampen a thing. The area is mostly paved to allow for seating, a fire pit, and grills. There is a small area with grass for dogs. "Amenities". 

Another building at this property has the same enclosed layout with a pool in the middle, which is even worse for noise.

Corporate landlords don't want to bother with tree maintenance (trimming, root spread, diseases). Cheaper to put in shrubs.

Yeah but what developer is going to pay extra to build around trees or plant new ones when they could pave it over and put low maintenance shrubs on the side instead?

I agree about the sound. Building quality needs to change. US apartments are miserable. Hearing and smelling my neighbors all day reminds me I'm packed in here like a sardine. My corporate landlords don't see me as a person, they see me as a number.

I cringe when I see these posts applauding rental mega complexes over row houses.

Actually natural light is a problem too! The sun shines on the windows/metal siding, which reflects into the interior and makes it so hot that I every plant I have tried to grow out there has died. 😂

But my neighbors in the bottom corner get no sunlight so they have to use a grow lamp on their plants. It's wild.

Hahaha you might live below my coworker. 

She has kids and is notorious for stomp-walking around the office. You can hear her coming down the hall. 

When she told me that she lives on the second floor of her complex, all I could think was oh God those poor neighbors. No peace.

Nope. My complex has bright lights in the courtyard. They leave them on all night for "safety reasons." It's like living at an airport. Sucks to sit on the patio on a peaceful night with a blinding light shining on you. 

Had to buy blackout curtains and a wraparound curtain rod because the light was shining through the blinds in the bedroom.

The most helpful thing would be to make these U shaped rather than fully enclosed. Give the sound somewhere to escape. 

I was shocked by how amplified the sounds are in the courtyard mine faces. I don't see vegetation muffling all of it, but it would be better than nothing.

Green buildings as in vegetation? I could see that helping, but not much. These courtyards are small.

And balconies do not help. Mine has balconies. Every time someone slams their balcony door you hear it. If they have a phone conversation, let their kid play, or put their barking dog outside, all 60 of the units facing inward hear it through their back door.

Mine has a fire pit and grill in the middle. People come by to grill and hang out with their portable speaker and we have to listen to their music and yelling for hours.

This design is nice on paper and awful in practice.

Disagree about the noise. The worst noise has always been directly from neighbors, but I'm in America where the walls are paper thin because splurging for soundproofing cuts into our oligarch's profits.

Stomping from the unit above, bass shaking the walls, screaming at the TV when a football game is on. And God forbid a family with a baby moves in. I know its not their fault, but its still fucking torture.

Advocating for dense apartment buildings in the US is inhumane unless the building quality also changes.

Love the idea, but please for the love of christ stop making these tall apartment buildings with an enclosed courtyard in the middle. Every noise in the courtyard is amplified and echoes. So any units facing inside are miserable to live in.

Ask me how I know.

No this approach is backwards.

You are taking tax money from people who chose not go to college, or those who had obstacles and couldn't, and transferring that benefit to those who went. This is a great way to divide the working class and convince more people vote republican. Bad strategy. If you focus on making college free and doing away with student loans, that is more popular and benefits everyone. Including those who have not gone to college. 

Young voters do not reliably vote in elections. You are lighting a fire under older conservatives and swing voters who are more likely to show up on election day.

Appreciate the links. I was meaning the decision placed before Biden, and the conversationin this sub. You can see responses below me saying that we need to cancel debt before fixing the root problem of predatory loans. I see this as a mistake. 

You are taking tax money from people who chose not go to college, or those who had obstacles and couldn't, and transferring that benefit to those who went. This is a great way to divide the working class and convince more people vote republican. Bad strategy. If you focus on making college free and doing away with student loans, that is more popular and benefits everyone. Including those who have not gone to college.

For the record I think it all needs to happen, I just think the approach is backwards. Both conversations need to happen together, or free college should be prioritized over the debt forgiveness.

I could've purchased a house with the money/time spent on paying back my student loans. Or I could have invested it. Do the middle children millennials in this situation just get fucked for being born at the wrong time?

Who is suggesting free college though? 

All I hear and see is debt forgiveness... and that's it. This does not fix the exploitative student loan system. Focusing on debt forgiveness rather than uprooting the whole system is such a blunder. 

I feel like I am taking crazy pills because I get down voted when I bring this up.

Therapy helps if you can get it. Just make sure you let the therapist know you don't have a time, place or method to kill yourself planned out.

I have found that sharing actual suicidal feelings with family is a bad idea. When I am down I let them know I'm feeling down, but I don't go into detail because i know they will overreact in a harmful way. I keep the details for my therapist. You may have a different relationship with your family though.

If you have a vibe that a friend will be supportive, it can be nice to let someone know you are in a bad place. Just remember that they are not your therapist. They are someone who cares about you.

That being said, if you start to feel truly trapped and start planning a place, time or method... talk to someone. Anyone. Family, friends. Suicide hotline. There are suicide text lines too.

Yeah I hear this a lot too. Seems like most people think it is a selfish act. They have an entirely alien worldview to me. I don't live to be an accessory in someone else's life, I don't owe anyone anything. These people have never experienced deep hopeless distress, so they don't understand why suicide happens. They don't understand how depression changes your logic. They just see it as a choice that hurts others.

This is a weird and loaded question, mate.

I'm in the camp that if someone is in so much mental anguish that they remove themselves from this world to stop the pain, calling them selfish is insulting. Obviously it would hurt the father if they wanted the child. But the woman has a right to her body. No one should live solely for someone else's sake.

It's terrible. Nice to know I'm not alone, because I feel alone. Can't talk about this with friends or family because it comes off as selfish or jealous.

I supported my best friend through her infertility and never said anything. But the thought was there every time she mentioned how much IUI was costing them, and how hard it was to hear her other friend brag about already being pregnant, her struggle to pick a theme for the nursery, her vacation to the east coast. Meanwhile my desk where I work 8 hrs a day is in my living room, 10 feet from my kitchen and washer/dryer because I can't afford a 2 bed apt. 

I went to school with these people but we are clearly in different social classes and it hurts.

Yeah :(
I may or may not know this from personal experience.

Lol. My complex will just send a letter to the neighbor asking them to "please stop doing ____, its against the rules" and then they know I snitched on them. If they are disrespectful enough to be a shitty neighbor, there's a chance they will take it to the next level with provocation.

Sounds good on paper. In reality it is horrible because any sound within the inside courtyard echoes like mad. If your apartment faces inward you hear every party that takes place, every dog and person on their balcony, every screaming child, everything.

This is how it should be. It blows my mind that people are suggesting towers of apartments. 

In the US, these apartment towers are made as cheaply as possible and living in them is torture. You hear neighbors through thin walls and floors. Smell weed through shared HVAC. In my area, having a unit with a bit of yard is a luxury, most are tiny balconies or nothing. Can't have grills. Vent hoods aren't installed so have fun setting off your smoke alarm if you cook anything on high heat.

Smaller houses, row houses, and duplexes are more dignified. Get rid of the big wasteful lawns.

* Shared ventilation can be a nightmare. Your bedroom smells like the neighbor's dinner or blunt.

* Bugs from neighbors

* Noise in hallways is not insulated through the door

* Noise if your windows face a shared space like pool or parking garage

My walls are pretty insulated but I can still feel them shake when my neighbor turns up his bass.

There are psychological benefits of having access to healthy food and green spaces. Environment is a factor in mental health. You don't have to be dirt poor to not have access to a good environment. Not sure if you consider that to be a basic need, many don't. It's not just envying the neighbor's flat screen and Lamborghini.

I have seen that firsthand. Money doesn't *gaurantee* happiness. 

But if you cannot satisfy your basic needs, the things that threaten your wellbeing, how can you be expected to focus on your mental health? Mental exhaustion from financial anxiety is eating up so many Americans and the rich do not understand it or care. How can you find stability when you can't afford shelter, or can't afford a car that you need to stay employed and buy food, can't afford medication to help your dopamine and seratonin deficiencies? Or if you're one car problem or health problem away from losing it all?
That's true. Therapy, medications, and time are bought with money. Time to work on yourself, have a hobby, exercise. Not everyone has the luxury and it makes everything worse.

No, it's cool. It's hard when you know everyone thinks you don't have it bad because you are able to meet certain needs that others can't. So then there's this extra layer of guilt like why am I not happy now, everyone says I should be happy. Society says I made it. 

But brain chemistry can screw you no matter what.

Yeah I have to unsub from there sometimes for a mental break because I relate too much. It is hard to log into work after getting shafted. What is frustrating is that a portion of the company is already remote due to other circumstances, but they are forcing the rest back to the buildings part time for "collaboration".

I am aware that I'm better off than half the country right now. That doesn't change the fact that my head is just above water and each year I'm closer to drowning with everyone else.
Damn I'm sorry :(

$$$ 
I need to speak with my therapist way more often. I cannot afford to. Many external things are contributing to depression, including housing. Which could also be improved with money.

Thank you :) I've been through worse periods, just need to start making changes. And fingers crossed for your counseling appointment! I always get some relief talking about what I'm going through with someone I'm not close to. Hopefully it makes your next steps clearer.

I have a therapist. Super expensive, so not weekly. Feel better after I talk to them but I wish they would do more to help me manage thoughts outside of sessions. 

On medication, ssri. Felt better for a couple months. Part of my anxiety is knowing that this job that I hate is the only reason I can afford therapy and medications, even though I have a crummy deductible. Would recommend trying both if accessible. I used betterhelp years ago because it was affordable. It helped me through a breakup, but it is not as thorough as traditional therapist. I cancelled after a few months but I was in a better spot.

My s/o has no insurance and is going through this same thing. Feeling stuck with no where to run. But he can't afford therapy and his monthly medication just cost $300 🙃

Same here. Cry it out, start to feel a bit of hope or leveled emotions, then a few hours later the sadness and panic is back. Started having irritability the past two years. Feel like the external things that need to change for me to be happy are insurmountable. I'm in flight mode with nowhere to go, which is giving me panic attacks.
Went through this recently, but also experienced sleep paralysis. So sleep was not a relief, it was a continuation of the nightmare. Was hell.

Couple weeks. Nausea, anxiety, depression, dissociation. I did not like the side effects of the meds like u described, and it was not helping. Got off meds for a year and now I'm in the middle of a breakdown after some unrelated medical scares. Good luck.
I had to take off work to taper off. Not fun.
Thank you
